title: "Q&A: TCEQ OSSF questions for rural North Texas"
category: "Q&A"
---

Ask anything about TCEQ OSSF permitting, conventional septic design, perc tests, drainfield sizing, or maintenance in Palo Pinto County and the surrounding counties.

I'm Tanner Coupland (Out West Septic, OS0041298). I do installs in the seven priority counties and I read the TCEQ Chapter 285 rules regularly. I'll answer what I can. For things I don't know, I'll say so.

**A few things to know before posting:**

- I'm an Installer I, not a DR (Designated Representative). I can explain the rules but I'm not the person who enforces them at your county.
- Out West Septic installs conventional gravity only. Aerobic questions get referred to Installer II contractors.
- The answer to many questions starts with "depends on your soil and your county" — please share both if relevant.

**Common question topics:**

- "How big does my tank need to be for N bedrooms?" — easy, the table answers it
- "Do I need a perc test?" — depends on whether this is new construction or repair
- "Can you put a system on a 0.5-acre lot?" — depends on the county and the setbacks
- "What does an install run in my county?" — depends on soil and access, but the cost estimator gives a planning range
- "How do I check if my existing system is permitted?" — call the county DR

I'll respond to most questions within 24 hours. For emergencies (a backup into the house or surfacing effluent), call your county DR first.
